   130→    # ── Cluster F: Security Density ──────────────────────────────────
   131→    security_hotspots = _build_security_hotspots(by_detector)
   132→    if security_hotspots:
   133→        evidence["security_hotspots"] = security_hotspots
   134→
   135→    # ── Cross-cutting: Signal density ────────────────────────────────
   136→    signal_density = _build_signal_density(by_file)
   137→    if signal_density:
   138→        evidence["signal_density"] = signal_density
   139→
   140→    # ── Systemic patterns ────────────────────────────────────────────
   141→    systemic = _build_systemic_patterns(smell_counter, smell_files)
   142→    if systemic:
   143→        evidence["systemic_patterns"] = systemic
   144→
   145→    return evidence
   146→
   147→
   148→# ── Cluster builders ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
   149→
   150→
   151→def _get_detail(finding: dict, key: str, default: Any = None) -> Any:
   152→    detail = finding.get("detail", {})
   153→    if not isinstance(detail, dict):
   154→        return default
   155→    return detail.get(key, default)
   156→
   157→
   158→def _get_signals(finding: dict) -> dict:
   159→    """Return the metrics dict for a finding.
   160→
   161→    Structural findings store metrics directly in ``detail`` (e.g. ``loc``,
   162→    ``complexity_score``).  Fall back to ``detail`` itself when the nested
   163→    ``signals`` key is absent so hotspot aggregation sees real values.
   164→    """
   165→    detail = finding.get("detail", {})
   166→    if not isinstance(detail, dict):
   167→        return {}
   168→    signals = detail.get("signals")
   169→    if isinstance(signals, dict):
   170→        return signals
   171→    return detail
   172→
   173→
   174→def _safe_num(value: Any, default: float = 0.0) -> float:
   175→    if isinstance(value, bool):
   176→        return default
   177→    if isinstance(value, int | float):
   178→        return float(value)
   179→    return default
   180→
   181→
   182→def _build_complexity_hotspots(
   183→    by_detector: dict[str, list[dict]],
   184→    by_file: dict[str, list[dict]],
   185→) -> list[dict]:
   186→    """Top 20 files by composite complexity score."""
   187→    # Gather per-file structural signals
   188→    file_data: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
   189→
   190→    for finding in by_detector.get("structural", []):
   191→        filepath = finding.get("file", "")
   192→        if not filepath:
   193→            continue
   194→        signals = _get_signals(finding)
   195→        entry = file_data.setdefault(filepath, {
   196→            "file": filepath, "loc": 0, "complexity_score": 0,
   197→            "signals": [], "component_count": 0, "function_count": 0,
   198→            "monster_functions": 0, "cyclomatic_hotspots": 0,
   199→        })
   200→        entry["loc"] = max(entry["loc"], _safe_num(signals.get("loc")))
   201→        entry["function_count"] = max(
   202→            entry["function_count"], _safe_num(signals.get("function_count"))
   203→        )
   204→        entry["component_count"] = max(
   205→            entry["component_count"], _safe_num(signals.get("component_count"))
   206→        )
   207→
   208→        # Collect notable signals
   209→        max_params = _safe_num(signals.get("max_params"))
   210→        if max_params >= 5:
   211→            entry["signals"].append(f"{int(max_params)} params")
   212→        max_nesting = _safe_num(signals.get("max_nesting"))
   213→        if max_nesting >= 4:
   214→            entry["signals"].append(f"nesting depth {int(max_nesting)}")
   215→        complexity = _safe_num(signals.get("complexity_score"))
   216→        entry["complexity_score"] = max(entry["complexity_score"], complexity)
   217→
   218→    # Enrich with smell findings for the same files
   219→    for finding in by_detector.get("smells", []):
   220→        filepath = finding.get("file", "")
   221→        smell_id = _get_detail(finding, "smell_id", "")
   222→        if filepath in file_data:
   223→            if smell_id == "monster_function":
   224→                file_data[filepath]["monster_functions"] += 1
   225→            elif smell_id in ("cyclomatic_complexity", "high_cyclomatic"):
   226→                file_data[filepath]["cyclomatic_hotspots"] += 1
   227→
   228→    # Also count responsibility_cohesion findings
   229→    for finding in by_detector.get("responsibility_cohesion", []):
   230→        filepath = finding.get("file", "")
   231→        if filepath in file_data:
   232→            clusters = _safe_num(_get_detail(finding, "cluster_count"))
   233→            file_data[filepath]["component_count"] = max(
   234→                file_data[filepath]["component_count"], clusters
   235→            )
   236→
   237→    # Composite score: loc/100 + complexity_score + component_count*3 + monster*10
   238→    for entry in file_data.values():
   239→        entry["_score"] = (
   240→            entry["loc"] / 100
   241→            + entry["complexity_score"]
   242→            + entry["component_count"] * 3
   243→            + entry["monster_functions"] * 10
   244→        )
   245→        # Deduplicate signals
   246→        entry["signals"] = list(dict.fromkeys(entry["signals"]))
   247→
   248→    ranked = sorted(file_data.values(), key=lambda e: -e["_score"])[:20]
   249→    for entry in ranked:
   250→        del entry["_score"]
   251→    return ranked
   252→
   253→
   254→def _build_error_hotspots(by_detector: dict[str, list[dict]]) -> list[dict]:
   255→    """Files with 3+ exception handling findings from smells detector."""
   256→    error_smell_ids = frozenset({
   257→        "broad_except", "silent_except", "empty_except",
   258→        "swallowed_error", "bare_except",
   259→    })
   260→    file_counts: dict[str, dict[str, int]] = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(int))
   261→
   262→    for finding in by_detector.get("smells", []):
   263→        smell_id = _get_detail(finding, "smell_id", "")
   264→        if smell_id not in error_smell_ids:
   265→            continue
   266→        filepath = finding.get("file", "")
   267→        if filepath:
   268→            file_counts[filepath][smell_id] += 1
   269→
   270→    results = []
   271→    for filepath, counts in file_counts.items():
   272→        total = sum(counts.values())
   273→        if total < 3:
   274→            continue
   275→        entry = {"file": filepath, "total": total}
   276→        for sid in sorted(error_smell_ids):
   277→            entry[sid] = counts.get(sid, 0)
   278→        results.append(entry)
   279→    results.sort(key=lambda e: -e["total"])
   280→    return results[:20]
   281→
   282→
   283→def _build_mutable_globals(by_detector: dict[str, list[dict]]) -> list[dict]:
   284→    """All global_mutable_config findings."""
   285→    results: list[dict] = []
   286→    file_data: dict[str, dict] = {}
   287→
   288→    for finding in by_detector.get("global_mutable_config", []):
   289→        filepath = finding.get("file", "")
   290→        if not filepath:
   291→            continue
   292→        entry = file_data.setdefault(filepath, {
   293→            "file": filepath, "names": [], "total_mutations": 0,
   294→        })
   295→        name = _get_detail(finding, "name", "")
   296→        if name and name not in entry["names"]:
   297→            entry["names"].append(name)
   298→        mutations = _safe_num(_get_detail(finding, "mutations"))
   299→        entry["total_mutations"] += int(mutations) if mutations else 1
   300→
   301→    results = sorted(file_data.values(), key=lambda e: -e["total_mutations"])
   302→    return results[:20]
   303→
   304→
   305→def _build_boundary_violations(by_detector: dict[str, list[dict]]) -> list[dict]:
   306→    """From coupling and layer_violation detectors."""
   307→    results: list[dict] = []
   308→    for det_name in ("coupling", "layer_violation"):
   309→        for finding in by_detector.get(det_name, []):
   310→            filepath = finding.get("file", "")
   311→            detail = finding.get("detail", {})
   312→            if not isinstance(detail, dict):
   313→                detail = {}
   314→            results.append({
   315→                "file": filepath,
   316→                "target": detail.get("target", detail.get("imported_from", "")),
   317→                "direction": detail.get("direction", detail.get("violation", "")),
   318→            })
   319→    return results[:30]
   320→
   321→
   322→def _build_dead_code(by_detector: dict[str, list[dict]]) -> list[dict]:
   323→    """Orphaned files + uncalled functions."""
   324→    results: list[dict] = []
   325→    for finding in by_detector.get("orphaned", []):
   326→        filepath = finding.get("file", "")
   327→        signals = _get_signals(finding)
   328→        loc = _safe_num(signals.get("loc", _get_detail(finding, "loc")))
   329→        results.append({"file": filepath, "kind": "orphaned", "loc": int(loc)})
   330→    for finding in by_detector.get("uncalled_functions", []):
   331→        filepath = finding.get("file", "")
   332→        detail = finding.get("detail", {})
   333→        loc = _safe_num(detail.get("loc", 0)) if isinstance(detail, dict) else 0
   334→        results.append({"file": filepath, "kind": "uncalled", "loc": int(loc)})
   335→    return results[:30]
   336→
   337→
   338→def _build_private_crossings(by_detector: dict[str, list[dict]]) -> list[dict]:
   339→    """From private_imports detector."""
   340→    results: list[dict] = []
   341→    for finding in by_detector.get("private_imports", []):
   342→        filepath = finding.get("file", "")
   343→        detail = finding.get("detail", {})
   344→        if not isinstance(detail, dict):
   345→            detail = {}
   346→        results.append({
   347→            "file": filepath,
   348→            "symbol": detail.get("symbol", detail.get("name", "")),
   349→            "source": detail.get("source", detail.get("imported_from", "")),
   350→            "target": detail.get("target", filepath),
   351→        })
   352→    return results[:30]
   353→
   354→
   355→def _build_deferred_import_density(by_file: dict[str, list[dict]]) -> list[dict]:
   356→    """Files with 2+ deferred_import smells (proxy for cycle pressure)."""
   357→    file_counts: dict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)
   358→    for filepath, file_findings in by_file.items():
   359→        for finding in file_findings:
   360→            if finding.get("detector") != "smells":
   361→                continue
   362→            if _get_detail(finding, "smell_id") == "deferred_import":
   363→                file_counts[filepath] += 1
   364→
   365→    results = [
   366→        {"file": filepath, "count": count}
   367→        for filepath, count in file_counts.items()
   368→        if count >= 2
   369→    ]
   370→    results.sort(key=lambda e: -e["count"])
   371→    return results[:20]
   372→
   373→
   374→def _build_duplicate_clusters(by_detector: dict[str, list[dict]]) -> list[dict]:
   375→    """From dupes and boilerplate_duplication detectors."""
   376→    results: list[dict] = []
   377→    for det_name in ("dupes", "boilerplate_duplication"):
   378→        for finding in by_detector.get(det_name, []):
   379→            detail = finding.get("detail", {})
   380→            if not isinstance(detail, dict):
   381→                detail = {}
   382→            kind = detail.get("kind", det_name)
   383→            name = detail.get("name", detail.get("function", finding.get("summary", "")[:60]))
   384→            files = detail.get("files", [])
   385→            if not isinstance(files, list) or not files:
   386→                fallback = finding.get("file", "")
   387→                files = [fallback] if fallback else []
   388→            results.append({
   389→                "kind": kind,
   390→                "cluster_size": len(files) if files else 1,
   391→                "name": name,
   392→                "files": files[:10],
   393→            })
   394→    return results[:20]
   395→
   396→
   397→def _build_naming_drift(by_detector: dict[str, list[dict]]) -> list[dict]:
   398→    """From naming detector."""
   399→    dir_data: dict[str, dict] = {}
   400→    for finding in by_detector.get("naming", []):
   401→        filepath = finding.get("file", "")
   402→        detail = finding.get("detail", {})
   403→        if not isinstance(detail, dict):
   404→            detail = {}
   405→        # Group by directory
   406→        parts = filepath.rsplit("/", 1)
   407→        directory = parts[0] + "/" if len(parts) > 1 else "./"
   408→        entry = dir_data.setdefault(directory, {
   409→            "directory": directory,
   410→            "majority": detail.get("expected_convention", ""),
   411→            "minority_count": 0,
   412→            "outliers": [],
   413→        })
   414→        entry["minority_count"] += 1
   415→        if filepath not in entry["outliers"]:
   416→            entry["outliers"].append(filepath)
   417→        if not entry["majority"] and detail.get("expected_convention"):
   418→            entry["majority"] = detail["expected_convention"]
   419→
   420→    results = sorted(dir_data.values(), key=lambda e: -e["minority_count"])
   421→    return results[:20]
   422→
   423→
   424→def _build_flat_dir_findings(by_detector: dict[str, list[dict]]) -> list[dict]:
   425→    """From flat_dirs detector."""
   426→    results: list[dict] = []
   427→    for finding in by_detector.get("flat_dirs", []):
   428→        filepath = finding.get("file", "")
   429→        detail = finding.get("detail", {})
   430→        if not isinstance(detail, dict):
   431→            detail = {}
   432→        results.append({
   433→            "directory": filepath,
   434→            "kind": detail.get("kind", detail.get("reason", "")),
   435→            "file_count": int(_safe_num(detail.get("file_count"))),
   436→            "combined_score": int(_safe_num(detail.get("score", detail.get("combined_score")))),
   437→        })
   438→    results.sort(key=lambda e: -e["combined_score"])
   439→    return results[:20]
   440→
   441→
   442→def _build_large_file_distribution(by_detector: dict[str, list[dict]]) -> dict | None:
   443→    """Distribution stats from structural findings."""
   444→    locs: list[float] = []
   445→    for finding in by_detector.get("structural", []):
   446→        signals = _get_signals(finding)
   447→        loc = _safe_num(signals.get("loc"))
   448→        if loc > 0:
   449→            locs.append(loc)
   450→    if not locs:
   451→        return None
   452→    locs.sort()
   453→    n = len(locs)
   454→    return {
   455→        "count": n,
   456→        "median_loc": int(locs[n // 2]),
   457→        "p90_loc": int(locs[int(n * 0.9)]) if n >= 10 else int(locs[-1]),
   458→        "p99_loc": int(locs[int(n * 0.99)]) if n >= 100 else int(locs[-1]),
   459→    }
   460→
   461→
   462→def _build_security_hotspots(by_detector: dict[str, list[dict]]) -> list[dict]:
   463→    """Files with 3+ security findings grouped by severity."""
   464→    file_counts: dict[str, dict[str, int]] = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(int))
   465→    for finding in by_detector.get("security", []):
   466→        filepath = finding.get("file", "")
   467→        if not filepath:
   468→            continue
   469→        detail = finding.get("detail", {})
   470→        severity = (
   471→            detail.get("severity", "medium")
   472→            if isinstance(detail, dict) else "medium"
   473→        )
   474→        file_counts[filepath][severity] += 1
   475→
   476→    results = []
   477→    for filepath, counts in file_counts.items():
   478→        total = sum(counts.values())
   479→        if total < 3:
   480→            continue
   481→        results.append({
   482→            "file": filepath,
   483→            "high_severity": counts.get("high", 0),
   484→            "medium_severity": counts.get("medium", 0),
   485→            "total": total,
   486→        })
   487→    results.sort(key=lambda e: (-e["high_severity"], -e["total"]))
   488→    return results[:20]
   489→
   490→
   491→def _build_signal_density(by_file: dict[str, list[dict]]) -> list[dict]:
   492→    """Top 20 files by number of distinct detectors firing."""
   493→    results: list[dict] = []
   494→    for filepath, file_findings in by_file.items():
   495→        detectors = set()
   496→        for finding in file_findings:
   497→            det = finding.get("detector", "")
   498→            if det:
   499→                detectors.add(det)
   500→        if len(detectors) >= 2:
   501→            results.append({
   502→                "file": filepath,
   503→                "detector_count": len(detectors),
   504→                "finding_count": len(file_findings),
   505→                "detectors": sorted(detectors),
   506→            })
   507→    results.sort(key=lambda e: (-e["detector_count"], -e["finding_count"]))
   508→    return results[:20]
   509→
   510→
   511→def _build_systemic_patterns(
   512→    smell_counter: Counter[str],
   513→    smell_files: dict[str, list[str]],
   514→) -> list[dict]:
   515→    """Smell subtypes appearing in 5+ files."""
   516→    results: list[dict] = []
   517→    for smell_id, count in smell_counter.most_common():
   518→        unique_files = sorted(set(smell_files.get(smell_id, [])))
   519→        if len(unique_files) < 5:
   520→            continue
   521→        # Find top hotspot files (most occurrences)
   522→        file_counts = Counter(smell_files[smell_id])
   523→        hotspots = [
   524→            f"{f} ({c})" for f, c in file_counts.most_common(5)
   525→        ]
   526→        results.append({
   527→            "pattern": smell_id,
   528→            "file_count": len(unique_files),
   529→            "hotspots": hotspots,
   530→        })
   531→    return results[:20]
   532→

## **Finding 1: fc72f362 - "Edge auth check can be bypassed by unrelated auth token usage elsewhere in file"**

### **Files with Relevant Detection Logic:**
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/languages/typescript/detectors/security.py` (lines 277-290, 298-302)
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/intelligence/review/context_signals/auth.py` (lines 153-163)

### **The Specific Problem:**

**Current detection code (security.py, lines 277-290):**
```python
if _looks_like_edge_handler(normalized_path, content):
    if not _AUTH_CHECK_RE.search(content):
        file_findings.append(
            _make_security_entry(
                filepath,
                1,
                content.splitlines()[0] if lines else "",
                check_id="edge_function_missing_auth",
                summary="Edge function serves requests without authentication check",
                severity="high",
                confidence="medium",
                remediation="Add authentication check (e.g., authenticateRequest, auth.getUser)",
            )
        )
```

**The auth check pattern (line 40-42):**
```python
_AUTH_CHECK_RE = re.compile(
    r"(?:authenticateRequest|auth\.getUser|supabase\.auth(?:\.getUser)?|verifyToken)",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
```

**The problem:** This is a **file-level check only**. It searches the entire file content for `_AUTH_CHECK_RE` and flags the file if no auth pattern is found anywhere. This has a critical flaw:

**Concrete example showing the vulnerability:**
```typescript
// /functions/orders.ts
import { serve } from "https://deno.land/std/http/server.ts";

// Unrelated utility function with auth check
function validateAdminToken(token: string) {
  const user = auth.getUser(token);  // <-- auth.getUser mentioned here!
  return user?.role === "admin";
}

// Actual edge handler with NO auth check
serve(async (req) => {
  const orders = await supabase.from("orders").select("*");
  return new Response(JSON.stringify(orders));
});
```

In this case:
- `_AUTH_CHECK_RE.search(content)` finds `auth.getUser` in the utility function
- The edge handler is NOT flagged, even though the actual request handler has no auth protection
- An attacker can call the edge function endpoint directly without authentication

**Why it's a problem:** The current detection doesn't distinguish between auth checks that actually protect the served handler and auth checks that exist elsewhere in the file (imports, utility functions, unrelated handlers, etc.).

### **Concrete Fix:**

The detection needs to:
1. Parse the file to identify handler boundaries (via `serve()` calls or exported handler functions)
2. Check for auth patterns **within each handler's scope** (nested inside the serve callback or handler function body)
3. Only pass if auth is found inside the handler's actual code path, not just in the file

**Example of what the fix should detect:**
```typescript
// GOOD - auth check INSIDE handler
serve(async (req) => {
  const user = await auth.getUser(req);
  if (!user) return new Response("Unauthorized", { status: 401 });
  
  const orders = await supabase.from("orders").select("*");
  return new Response(JSON.stringify(orders));
});

// BAD - auth check OUTSIDE handler (current code misses this)
function validateToken(t) { auth.getUser(t); }
serve(async (req) => {  // <-- Should flag this
  const orders = await supabase.from("orders").select("*");
  return new Response(JSON.stringify(orders));
});
```

## **Finding 2: e17679b4 - "RLS coverage heuristics miss quoted/schema-qualified table definitions"**

### **Files with Relevant Detection Logic:**
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/intelligence/review/context_signals/auth.py` (lines 24-31)
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/languages/typescript/detectors/security.py` (lines 354-373)

### **The Specific Problem:**

**Current table matching pattern (auth.py, lines 24-25):**
```python
_RLS_TABLE_RE = re.compile(
    r"CREATE\s+TABLE\s+(?:IF\s+NOT\s+EXISTS\s+)?(\w+)", re.IGNORECASE
)
```

**The RLS enable pattern (auth.py, lines 27-31):**
```python
_RLS_ENABLE_RE = re.compile(
    r"ALTER\s+TABLE\s+(\w+)\s+ENABLE\s+ROW\s+LEVEL\s+SECURITY"
    r"|CREATE\s+POLICY\s+\w+\s+ON\s+(\w+)",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
```

**Current logic in auth.py (lines 116-121):**
```python
# RLS coverage (SQL/migration files)
for match in _RLS_TABLE_RE.finditer(content):
    rls_tables.add(match.group(1))  # Captures table name
for match in _RLS_ENABLE_RE.finditer(content):
    table = match.group(1) or match.group(2)
    if table:
        rls_enabled.add(table)
```

**The problem:** Both patterns only capture `\w+` (alphanumeric + underscore), which means they fail to match:

### **Concrete examples showing the vulnerability:**

**Example 1: Quoted table names**
```sql
CREATE TABLE "User_Profiles" (...)  -- Double quotes (PostgreSQL standard)
CREATE TABLE `order_items` (...)    -- Backticks (MySQL)
CREATE TABLE [archived_orders] (...) -- Square brackets (SQL Server)

ALTER TABLE "User_Profiles" ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
```

**Problem:** The pattern `(\w+)` doesn't match `"User_Profiles"`, so:
- `rls_tables` gets nothing from `CREATE TABLE "User_Profiles"`
- Even though RLS is enabled, the table name won't match
- Result: False negative - table appears unprotected

**Example 2: Schema-qualified table names**
```sql
CREATE TABLE public.users (...)       -- Schema-qualified
CREATE TABLE auth.user_profiles (...) -- Another schema
CREATE TABLE "app"."settings" (...)   -- Quoted schema

ALTER TABLE public.users ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE "app"."settings" ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
```

**Problem:** The patterns don't handle schema prefixes:
- `CREATE TABLE public.users` → only captures `users` if at all (depends on position)
- The actual pattern expects `CREATE TABLE` followed immediately by the name
- The qualifiers prevent matching

**Example 3: Mixed quoted and schema-qualified**
```sql
CREATE TABLE "auth"."user_sessions" (...)
ALTER TABLE "auth"."user_sessions" ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
```

This will completely fail to match with current patterns.

### **Concrete Fix:**

The patterns need to be updated to:

**For table creation:**
```python
# Original:
_RLS_TABLE_RE = re.compile(
    r"CREATE\s+TABLE\s+(?:IF\s+NOT\s+EXISTS\s+)?(\w+)", re.IGNORECASE
)

# Fixed version should capture:
_RLS_TABLE_RE = re.compile(
    r"CREATE\s+TABLE\s+(?:IF\s+NOT\s+EXISTS\s+)?"
    r"(?:(?:[\w\"]+)\.)?[\w\"`\[\]]+",  # schema.table or just table, with quotes/brackets
    re.IGNORECASE
)
```

Or better yet, a more robust approach:
```python
# Capture quoted and unquoted names separately, normalize to canonical form
_RLS_TABLE_RE = re.compile(
    r"CREATE\s+TABLE\s+(?:IF\s+NOT\s+EXISTS\s+)?"
    r"(?:(?:[\w\"]+)\.)?"              # Optional schema prefix (with quotes)
    r"((?:\"[^\"]+\"|`[^`]+`|\[[^\]]+\]|\w+))",  # Table name (quoted or unquoted)
    re.IGNORECASE
)

# Then normalize captured names by stripping quotes
def _normalize_table_name(quoted_name: str) -> str:
    """Strip quotes from table names for comparison."""
    if quoted_name.startswith('"') and quoted_name.endswith('"'):
        return quoted_name[1:-1]
    if quoted_name.startswith('`') and quoted_name.endswith('`'):
        return quoted_name[1:-1]
    if quoted_name.startswith('[') and quoted_name.endswith(']'):
        return quoted_name[1:-1]
    return quoted_name
```

**For RLS enable/policy creation:**
```python
# Original:
_RLS_ENABLE_RE = re.compile(
    r"ALTER\s+TABLE\s+(\w+)\s+ENABLE\s+ROW\s+LEVEL\s+SECURITY"
    r"|CREATE\s+POLICY\s+\w+\s+ON\s+(\w+)",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)

# Fixed version should handle schema.table and quoted names:
_RLS_ENABLE_RE = re.compile(
    r"ALTER\s+TABLE\s+"
    r"(?:(?:[\w\"]+)\.)?(?:\"[^\"]+\"|`[^`]+`|\[[^\]]+\]|\w+)"  # Table reference
    r"\s+ENABLE\s+ROW\s+LEVEL\s+SECURITY"
    r"|CREATE\s+POLICY\s+\w+\s+ON\s+"
    r"(?:(?:[\w\"]+)\.)?(?:\"[^\"]+\"|`[^`]+`|\[[^\]]+\]|\w+)",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
```

**Then in the gathering logic (auth.py lines 116-121):**
```python
# RLS coverage (SQL/migration files)
tables_created = {}
tables_enabled = {}

for match in _RLS_TABLE_RE.finditer(content):
    raw_name = match.group(1)
    normalized = _normalize_table_name(raw_name)
    tables_created[normalized] = raw_name

for match in _RLS_ENABLE_RE.finditer(content):
    # Extract table name, handling both group(1) and group(2)
    raw_name = match.group(1) or match.group(2)
    if raw_name:
        normalized = _normalize_table_name(raw_name)
        tables_enabled.add(normalized)

# Now rls_with and rls_without use normalized names
rls_with = sorted(tables_created.keys() & tables_enabled)
rls_without = sorted(tables_created.keys() - tables_enabled)
```

    20→def _enable_live_review_output() -> None:
    21→    """Best-effort: force line-buffered review output for non-TTY runners."""
    22→    for stream_name in ("stdout", "stderr"):
    23→        stream = getattr(sys, stream_name, None)
    24→        reconfigure = getattr(stream, "reconfigure", None)
    25→        if not callable(reconfigure):
    26→            continue
    27→        try:
    28→            reconfigure(line_buffering=True, write_through=True)
    29→        except (OSError, ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
    30→            _ = exc
    31→
    32→
    33→def _require_lang_or_exit(lang) -> None:
    34→    if lang:
    35→        return
    36→    print(
    37→        colorize("  Error: could not detect language. Use --lang.", "red"),
    38→        file=sys.stderr,
    39→    )
    40→    sys.exit(1)
    41→
    42→
    43→def _mode_flags(args: argparse.Namespace) -> tuple[list[bool], object, object]:

    45→    run_batches = bool(getattr(args, "run_batches", False))

1→"""Path resolution and exclusion matching helpers."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import os
     6→import tempfile
     7→import fnmatch
     8→from pathlib import Path
     9→
    10→from desloppify.core._internal.text_utils import get_project_root
    11→
    12→
    13→def matches_exclusion(rel_path: str, exclusion: str) -> bool:
    14→    """Check if a relative path matches an exclusion pattern."""
    15→    parts = Path(rel_path).parts
    16→    if exclusion in parts:
    17→        return True
    18→    if "*" in exclusion:
    19→        if any(fnmatch.fnmatch(part, exclusion) for part in parts):
    20→            return True
    21→        # Full-path glob match for patterns with directory separators
    22→        # (e.g. "Wan2GP/**" should match "Wan2GP/models/rf.py").
    23→        if "/" in exclusion or os.sep in exclusion:
    24→            normalized_path = rel_path.lstrip("./")
    25→            if fnmatch.fnmatch(normalized_path, exclusion):
    26→                return True
    27→    if "/" in exclusion or os.sep in exclusion:
    28→        normalized = exclusion.rstrip("/").rstrip(os.sep)
    29→        return rel_path.startswith(normalized + "/") or rel_path.startswith(
    30→            normalized + os.sep
    31→        )
    32→    return False
    33→
    34→
    35→def normalize_path_separators(path: str) -> str:
    36→    return path.replace("\\", "/")
    37→
    38→
    39→def safe_relpath(path: str | Path, start: str | Path) -> str:
    40→    try:
    41→        return os.path.relpath(str(path), str(start))
    42→    except ValueError:
    43→        return str(Path(path).resolve())
    44→
    45→
    46→def rel(path: str) -> str:
    47→    root = get_project_root()
    48→    resolved = Path(path).resolve()
    49→    try:
    50→        return normalize_path_separators(str(resolved.relative_to(root)))

## Summary of Cross-Module Architecture Findings

Based on my investigation, here are the concrete details for both cross_module_architecture findings:

### **Finding 1: Private `core._internal` utilities consumed cross-layer (ID: 97d8fb09)**

#### Specific Imports from `_internal`:

The `_internal` package exports 2 modules with heavily used utilities:

**`text_utils.py`** (most imported):
- `PROJECT_ROOT` (module-level constant) - 37 direct imports
- `get_project_root()` - 12 direct imports
- `is_numeric()` - 9 direct imports
- `get_area()` - 8 direct imports
- `strip_c_style_comments()` - 5 direct imports

**`coercions.py`**:
- `coerce_positive_int()` - 3 direct imports
- `coerce_confidence()` - 2 direct imports
- `coerce_non_negative_float()` - multiple via policy.py
- `coerce_positive_float()` - multiple via policy.py
- `coerce_non_negative_int()` - multiple via policy.py

#### Where These Are Imported From:

The imports cross multiple layers:

**Cross-layer imports (problem area):**
1. **App Commands Layer** (`desloppify/app/commands/`):
   - `/app/commands/helpers/lang.py` - imports `PROJECT_ROOT`
   - `/app/commands/helpers/score.py` - imports `is_numeric`
   - `/app/commands/helpers/state.py` - imports `PROJECT_ROOT`
   - `/app/commands/review/batch.py` - imports `coerce_positive_int`, `get_project_root`
   - `/app/commands/review/external.py` - imports `coerce_positive_int`, `get_project_root`
   - `/app/commands/review/import_helpers.py` - imports `get_project_root`
   - `/app/commands/review/prepare.py` - imports `coerce_positive_int`
   - `/app/commands/review/runtime/policy.py` - imports multiple coercion functions
   - `/app/commands/scan/*.py` - multiple files import `PROJECT_ROOT`
   - `/app/commands/status_parts/render.py` - imports `get_area`
   - `/app/commands/update_skill.py` - imports `get_project_root`
   - `/app/output/scorecard.py` - imports `PROJECT_ROOT`

2. **Language Plugins Layer** (`desloppify/languages/`):
   - All language `__init__.py` files - import `get_area`
   - Language detectors (`python/`, `typescript/`, `dart/`) - import `PROJECT_ROOT`, `strip_c_style_comments`
   - Multiple extractors - import `PROJECT_ROOT`, `strip_c_style_comments`

3. **Engine Layer** (`desloppify/engine/`):
   - Scoring modules - import `is_numeric`, `coerce_confidence`
   - State modules - import `is_numeric`
   - Planning modules - import `PROJECT_ROOT`

4. **Intelligence/Review Layer** (`desloppify/intelligence/review/`):
   - Review dimensions modules - import `is_numeric`

5. **CLI Entry** (`desloppify/cli.py`) - imports `get_project_root`

#### Existing Public APIs:

There **are** some public API re-export modules, but they're incomplete:
- `/core/paths_api.py` - imports `text_utils.get_project_root` and `text_utils.PROJECT_ROOT` but ONLY re-exports them internally (not in `__all__`)
- `/core/grep.py` - imports `text_utils` as `_text_utils` for internal use
- `/core/paths_api.py` - same pattern
- `/core/config.py`, `/core/file_paths.py`, `/core/query_paths.py`, `/core/skill_docs.py`, `/core/source_discovery.py` - all import directly from `_internal`

**What's missing:** There's no public facade API that re-exports these utilities. The pattern shows that internal modules in `core/` itself are importing from `_internal`, and then external layers (commands, languages, engine) are doing the same.

#### What Needs to Change:

1. **Create explicit public utility API modules** in `core/`:
   - `core/text_utils_api.py` or `core/text_api.py` - public re-export of text utilities
   - `core/coercions_api.py` - public re-export of coercion functions
   - Both should have complete `__all__` exports

2. **Migrate all internal imports** from `_internal` to use the new public APIs:
   - Within `core/`: Change internal modules to use the public APIs instead of reaching into `_internal`
   - In `app/commands/`: Update all 9+ files to import from public APIs
   - In `languages/`: Update all language modules to import from public APIs
   - In `engine/`: Update scoring/state/planning modules
   - In `intelligence/review/`: Update dimension modules

3. **Keep `_internal` private** by removing external access (documentation/enforcement)

---

### **Finding 2: Review command package wiring creates cycle-prone imports (ID: b470ec46)**

#### Current Structure:

The review command is split across two layers:

**App Command Layer** (`desloppify/app/commands/review/`):
- `__init__.py` → exports `cmd_review`
- `entrypoint.py` → entry point, imports from `.batch`, `.external`, `.import_cmd`, `.merge`, `.preflight`, `.prepare`
- `batch.py` → imports from `.batch_core`, `.batches`, `.runtime`
- `external.py` → imports from `.runtime`
- `runtime/__init__.py` → lazy-loads `runtime.setup` and `runtime.policy`
- `runtime/policy.py` → imports coercions from `core._internal`
- `runtime/setup.py` → imports language runtime modules

**Intelligence Layer** (`desloppify/intelligence/review/`):
- `__init__.py` → re-exports 40+ public functions and classes from submodules
- Core submodules: `context`, `policy`, `prepare`, `importing`, `dimensions`, `selection`, `remediation`

#### Current Data Flow (No Actual Cycles Found):

- `app/commands/review/entrypoint.py` imports from:
  - `.batch`, `.external`, `.import_cmd`, `.merge`, `.preflight`, `.prepare` (all in same package)
  - `desloppify.intelligence.review` (reads from intelligence layer)

- `app/commands/review/batch.py` imports from:
  - `.batch_core`, `.batches`, `.runner_helpers`, `.runtime` (local review module imports)
  - `desloppify.intelligence.review` (intelligence layer)

- `desloppify.intelligence.review/__init__.py` imports from:
  - Internal submodules (`.context`, `.dimensions`, `.policy`, etc.)
  - NO imports from `desloppify.app.commands.review` (verified - no backlinks)

#### The Real Risks (Cycle-Prone Patterns):

1. **Deep internal sub-package imports in app/commands/review**:
   - `batch.py` imports from `.batches` which imports from `runtime.policy`
   - `runtime/policy.py` has isolated imports from `core._internal.coercions` but could become entangled

2. **Package root wiring via `__init__.py`**:
   - `app/commands/review/__init__.py` uses a simple re-export pattern (just `cmd_review`)
   - But the entrypoint imports 6 functions from sibling modules (`.batch`, `.external`, `.import_cmd`, etc.)
   - If any of these imported functions later tried to import something from the package root, you'd get a cycle

3. **Lazy-loading pattern in `runtime/__init__.py`**:
   ```python
   _LAZY_EXPORTS = {
       "runner_helpers": "desloppify.app.commands.review.runner_helpers",
       "policy": ".policy",
   }
   def __getattr__(name: str):
       # lazy loads at runtime
   ```
   This defers import errors and could mask circular dependencies

4. **Intelligence layer interface breadth**:
   - `/intelligence/review/__init__.py` exports 40+ names from 8+ submodules
   - Any of these submodules could theoretically import back to `app/commands/review` (currently they don't, but it's a risk)

#### Specific Import Paths That Could Become Problematic:

1. **Import chain**: `entrypoint.py` → `.batch` → `.batches` → `.runtime.policy`
   - If `.runtime.policy` ever needs to import from entrypoint or sibling modules, cycle forms

2. **Lazy-loading defers detection**: `runtime/__init__.py` uses `__getattr__` which defers import resolution
   - Makes it harder to detect circular dependencies at module load time
   - Could fail at runtime when `runtime.policy` is first accessed

3. **Cross-package wiring risk**: `batch.py` imports `do_import` from `.import_cmd`
   - `import_cmd.py` imports from `desloppify.intelligence.review`
   - If intelligence.review grows and needs `app.commands.review` utilities, cycle forms

#### What Needs to Change:

1. **Flatten the runtime subpackage**:
   - Move `runtime/setup.py` functions directly into a `review_runtime.py` module
   - Move `runtime/policy.py` into a separate `batch_policy.py` module
   - Eliminate the `runtime/__init__.py` lazy-loading pattern
   - Make all imports explicit and upfront (easier to detect cycles)

2. **Create explicit internal interfaces**:
   - Define what `batch.py`, `external.py`, `import_cmd.py` actually need to share
   - Create a separate `_batch_shared.py` or `_internal.py` within review package for shared helpers
   - Avoid importing full modules from entrypoint

3. **Prevent backimports from intelligence/review**:
   - Add a lint rule or documentation that intelligence/review MUST NOT import from app/commands
   - Currently enforced by convention only - make it explicit

4. **Document dependency boundaries**:
   - `app/commands/review/` is orchestration: calls intelligence/review and language runtime
   - `intelligence/review/` is pure logic: no command/orchestration imports
   - Enforce this architecture at CI time

5. **Eliminate lazy-loading in runtime**:
   Replace the `__getattr__` pattern with normal imports so:
   - Circular dependencies are detected at import time, not runtime
   - Tools like `python -m py_compile` can verify module structure
   - Developers see import errors immediately during development

---

## Summary Table

| Finding | Root Cause | Scope | Impact |
|---------|-----------|-------|--------|
| **_internal cross-layer** | No public API facades | 70+ files across 5 layers | Difficult to refactor `_internal`; tight coupling to private internals |
| **Review command wiring** | Package root indirection + lazy-loading + broad interface | 8+ review submodules + 40+ exported names | Hard to detect circular dependencies; refactoring risk when intelligence grows |

   210→
   211→    @staticmethod
   212→    def _clone_default(default: object) -> object:
   213→        return copy.deepcopy(default)
   214→
   215→    @classmethod
   216→    def _coerce_value(cls, raw: object, expected: type, default: object) -> object:
   217→        """Best-effort coercion for config/CLI values."""
   218→        fallback = cls._clone_default(default)
   219→        if raw is None:
   220→            return fallback
   221→
   222→        if expected is bool:
   223→            if isinstance(raw, bool):
   224→                return raw
   225→            if isinstance(raw, str):
   226→                lowered = raw.strip().lower()
   227→                if lowered in {"1", "true", "yes", "on"}:
   228→                    return True
   229→                if lowered in {"0", "false", "no", "off"}:
   230→                    return False
   231→                return fallback
   232→            if is_numeric(raw):
   233→                return bool(raw)
   234→            return fallback
   235→
   236→        if expected is int:
   237→            if isinstance(raw, bool):
   238→                return fallback
   239→            if is_numeric(raw):
   240→                return int(raw)
   241→            try:
   242→                return int(raw)
   243→            except (TypeError, ValueError):
   244→                return fallback
   245→
   246→        if expected is float:
   247→            if isinstance(raw, bool):
   248→                return fallback
   249→            if is_numeric(raw):
   250→                return float(raw)
   251→            try:
   252→                return float(raw)
   253→            except (TypeError, ValueError):
   254→                return fallback
   255→
   256→        if expected is str:
   257→            return raw if isinstance(raw, str) else str(raw)
   258→
   259→        if expected is list:
   260→            return raw if isinstance(raw, list) else fallback
   261→
   262→        if expected is dict:
   263→            return raw if isinstance(raw, dict) else fallback
   264→
   265→        return raw if isinstance(raw, expected) else fallback
   266→
   267→    def normalize_settings(self, values: dict[str, object] | None) -> dict[str, object]:
   268→        values = values if isinstance(values, dict) else {}
   269→        normalized: dict[str, object] = {}
   270→        for key, spec in self.setting_specs.items():
   271→            raw = values.get(key, spec.default)
   272→            normalized[key] = self._coerce_value(raw, spec.type, spec.default)
   273→        return normalized
   274→
   275→    def normalize_runtime_options(
   276→        self,
   277→        values: dict[str, object] | None,
   278→        *,
   279→        strict: bool = False,
   280→    ) -> dict[str, object]:
   281→        values = values if isinstance(values, dict) else {}
   282→        specs = self.runtime_option_specs
   283→        if strict:
   284→            unknown = sorted(set(values) - set(specs))
   285→            if unknown:
   286→                raise KeyError(
   287→                    f"Unknown runtime option(s) for {self.name}: {', '.join(unknown)}"
   288→                )
   289→        normalized: dict[str, object] = {}
   290→        for key, spec in specs.items():
   291→            raw = values.get(key, spec.default)
   292→            normalized[key] = self._coerce_value(raw, spec.type, spec.default)
   293→        return normalized
   294→
   295→    def set_runtime_context(
   296→        self,
   297→        *,
   298→        settings: dict[str, object] | None = None,
   299→        options: dict[str, object] | None = None,
   300→    ) -> None:
   301→        """Set default runtime settings/options for future LangRun creation."""
   302→        if settings is not None:
   303→            self._default_runtime_settings = self.normalize_settings(settings)
   304→        if options is not None:
   305→            self._default_runtime_options = self.normalize_runtime_options(options)
   306→
   307→    def runtime_setting(self, key: str, default: Any = None) -> Any:
   308→        """Read setting from config-level runtime defaults."""
   309→        if key in self._default_runtime_settings:
   310→            return copy.deepcopy(self._default_runtime_settings[key])
   311→        spec = self.setting_specs.get(key)
   312→        if spec:
   313→            return copy.deepcopy(spec.default)
   314→        return default
   315→
   316→    def runtime_option(self, key: str, default: Any = None) -> Any:
   317→        """Read option from config-level runtime defaults."""
   318→        if key in self._default_runtime_options:
   319→            return copy.deepcopy(self._default_runtime_options[key])
   320→        spec = self.runtime_option_specs.get(key)
   321→        if spec:
   322→            return copy.deepcopy(spec.default)
   323→        return default
   324→
   325→    def detect_lang_security(
   326→        self, files: list[str], zone_map: FileZoneMap | None
   327→    ) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:

   329→        return [], 0

    57→def phase_dupes(path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract) -> tuple[list[Finding], dict[str, int]]:
    58→    """Shared phase runner: detect duplicate functions via lang.extract_functions.
    59→
    60→    When a zone map is available, filters out functions from zone-excluded files
    61→    before the O(n^2) comparison to avoid test/config/generated false positives.
    62→    """
    63→    functions = lang.extract_functions(path)
    64→
    65→    # Filter out functions from zone-excluded files.
    66→    if lang.zone_map is not None:
    67→        before = len(functions)
    68→        functions = [
    69→            f
    70→            for f in functions
    71→            if lang.zone_map.get(getattr(f, "file", "")) not in EXCLUDED_ZONES
    72→        ]
    73→        excluded = before - len(functions)
    74→        if excluded:
    75→            log(f"         zones: {excluded} functions excluded (non-production)")
    76→
    77→    entries, total_functions = detect_duplicates(functions)
    78→    findings = make_dupe_findings(entries, log)
    79→    return findings, {"dupes": total_functions}

    82→def phase_boilerplate_duplication(
    83→    path: Path,

    87→    entries = detect_with_jscpd(path)

    90→    entries = _filter_boilerplate_entries_by_zone(entries, lang.zone_map)

    98→        )

   100→            loc_preview += f", +{len(locations) - 4} more"
   101→        findings.append(

   107→                confidence="medium",
   108→                summary=(
   109→                    f"Boilerplate block repeated across {entry['distinct_files']} files "
   110→                    f"(window {entry['window_size']} lines): {loc_preview}"
   111→                ),
   112→                detail={
   113→                    "distinct_files": entry["distinct_files"],
   114→                    "window_size": entry["window_size"],
   115→                    "locations": locations,
   116→                    "sample": entry["sample"],
   117→                },
   118→            )
   119→        )
   120→
   121→    if findings:
   122→        log(f"         boilerplate duplication: {len(findings)} clusters")
   123→    distinct_files = len({loc["file"] for e in entries for loc in e["locations"]})
   124→    return findings, {"boilerplate_duplication": distinct_files}

   126→
   127→def _filter_boilerplate_entries_by_zone(entries: list[dict], zone_map) -> list[dict]:
   128→    """Keep only in-scope, zone-allowed boilerplate clusters.
   129→
   130→    jscpd can return files that are outside language discovery (artifacts/docs).
   131→    Restricting to known zone-map files prevents unknown paths from being treated
   132→    as production findings.
   133→    """
   134→    if zone_map is None:
   135→        return entries
   136→
   137→    known_files = set(zone_map.all_files())
   138→    filtered: list[dict] = []
   139→    skipped = 0
   140→    for entry in entries:
   141→        locations = entry.get("locations", [])
   142→        kept_locations = [
   143→            loc
   144→            for loc in locations
   145→            if loc.get("file") in known_files
   146→            and not should_skip_finding(
   147→                zone_map,
   148→                loc.get("file", ""),
   149→                "boilerplate_duplication",
   150→            )
   151→        ]
   152→        distinct_files = {loc["file"] for loc in kept_locations}
   153→        if len(distinct_files) < 2:
   154→            skipped += 1
   155→            continue
   156→
   157→        normalized = dict(entry)
   158→        normalized["locations"] = sorted(
   159→            kept_locations,
   160→            key=lambda item: (item.get("file", ""), item.get("line", 0)),
   161→        )
   162→        normalized["distinct_files"] = len(distinct_files)
   163→        filtered.append(normalized)
   164→
   165→    if skipped:
   166→        log(f"         zones: {skipped} boilerplate clusters excluded")
   167→    return filtered

   170→def find_external_test_files(path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract) -> set[str]:
   171→    """Find test files in standard locations outside the scanned path."""
   172→    extra = set()
   173→    path_root = path.resolve()
   174→    project_root = get_project_root()
   175→    test_dirs = lang.external_test_dirs or ["tests", "test"]
   176→    exts = tuple(lang.test_file_extensions or lang.extensions)
   177→    for test_dir in test_dirs:
   178→        d = project_root / test_dir
   179→        if not d.is_dir():
   180→            continue
   181→        if d.resolve().is_relative_to(path_root):
   182→            continue  # test_dir is inside scanned path, zone_map already has it
   183→        for root, _, files in os.walk(d):
   184→            for filename in files:
   185→                if any(filename.endswith(ext) for ext in exts):
   186→                    extra.add(os.path.join(root, filename))
   187→    return extra

   239→def _merge_detector_coverage(
   240→    existing: dict[str, object],
   241→    incoming: dict[str, object],
   242→) -> dict[str, object]:
   243→    merged = dict(existing)
   244→    merged["status"] = (
   245→        "reduced"
   246→        if str(existing.get("status", "full")) == "reduced"
   247→        or str(incoming.get("status", "full")) == "reduced"
   248→        else "full"
   249→    )
   250→    merged["confidence"] = round(
   251→        min(
   252→            coerce_confidence(existing.get("confidence")),
   253→            coerce_confidence(incoming.get("confidence")),
   254→        ),
   255→        2,
   256→    )
   257→
   258→    for key in ("summary", "impact", "remediation", "tool", "reason"):
   259→        current = str(merged.get(key, "") or "").strip()
   260→        update = str(incoming.get(key, "") or "").strip()
   261→        if update and not current:
   262→            merged[key] = update
   263→        elif update and current and update not in current:
   264→            merged[key] = f"{current} | {update}"
   265→    return merged
   266→
   267→
   268→def _record_detector_coverage(lang: LangRuntimeContract, coverage: DetectorCoverageStatus | None) -> None:
   269→    if coverage is None:
   270→        return
   271→    normalized = _coverage_to_dict(coverage)
   272→    detector = str(normalized.get("detector", "")).strip()
   273→    if not detector:
   274→        return
   275→    existing = lang.detector_coverage.get(detector)
   276→    if isinstance(existing, dict):
   277→        lang.detector_coverage[detector] = _merge_detector_coverage(existing, normalized)
   278→    else:
   279→        lang.detector_coverage[detector] = normalized
   280→

   282→def phase_security(path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract) -> tuple[list[Finding], dict[str, int]]:
   283→    """Shared phase: detect security issues (cross-language + lang-specific)."""
   284→    zone_map = lang.zone_map
   285→    files = lang.file_finder(path) if lang.file_finder else []
   286→    entries, cross_lang_scanned = detect_security_issues(
   287→        files,
   288→        zone_map,
   289→        lang.name,
   290→        scan_root=path,
   291→    )
   292→    lang_scanned = 0
   293→
   294→    # Also call lang-specific security detectors.
   295→    lang_result = lang.detect_lang_security_detailed(files, zone_map)
   296→    if isinstance(lang_result, LangSecurityResult):
   297→        lang_entries = lang_result.entries
   298→        lang_scanned = max(0, int(lang_result.files_scanned))
   299→        _record_detector_coverage(lang, lang_result.coverage)
   300→    else:
   301→        # Backwards compatibility for legacy plugins returning tuple[list[dict], int].
   302→        lang_entries, legacy_scanned = lang_result
   303→        lang_scanned = max(0, int(legacy_scanned or 0))
   304→    entries.extend(lang_entries)
   305→
   306→    entries = filter_entries(zone_map, entries, "security")
   307→    potential = max(cross_lang_scanned, lang_scanned)
   308→
   309→    results = _entries_to_findings(
   310→        "security",
   311→        entries,
   312→        include_zone=True,
   313→        zone_map=zone_map,
   314→    )
   315→    _log_phase_summary("security", results, potential, "files scanned")
   316→
   317→    if "security" not in lang.detector_coverage:
   318→        lang.detector_coverage["security"] = {
   319→            "detector": "security",
   320→            "status": "full",
   321→            "confidence": 1.0,
   322→            "summary": "Security coverage complete for enabled detectors.",
   323→            "impact": "",
   324→            "remediation": "",
   325→            "tool": "",
   326→            "reason": "",
   327→        }
   328→
   329→    return results, {"security": potential}

   332→def phase_test_coverage(
   333→    path: Path,

   337→    zone_map = lang.zone_map

   375→def phase_subjective_review(
   376→    path: Path,
   377→    lang: LangRuntimeContract,
   378→) -> tuple[list[Finding], dict[str, int]]:
   379→    """Shared phase: detect files missing subjective design review."""
   380→    zone_map = lang.zone_map
   381→    max_age = lang.review_max_age_days
   382→    files = lang.file_finder(path) if lang.file_finder else []
   383→    review_cache = lang.review_cache
   384→    if isinstance(review_cache, dict) and "files" in review_cache:
   385→        per_file_cache = review_cache.get("files", {})
   386→    else:
   387→        # Legacy format: flat dict of file entries with no "files" wrapper.
   388→        # Filter out known top-level structural keys so they aren't treated as
   389→        # file paths, then reconstruct the canonical shape preserving them.
   390→        _TOP_LEVEL_KEYS = frozenset({"holistic"})
   391→        raw = review_cache if isinstance(review_cache, dict) else {}
   392→        per_file_cache = {k: v for k, v in raw.items() if k not in _TOP_LEVEL_KEYS}
   393→        review_cache = {"files": per_file_cache}
   394→        if "holistic" in raw:
   395→            review_cache["holistic"] = raw["holistic"]
   396→
   397→    entries, potential = detect_review_coverage(
   398→        files,
   399→        zone_map,
   400→        per_file_cache,
   401→        lang.name,
   402→        low_value_pattern=lang.review_low_value_pattern,
   403→        max_age_days=max_age,
   404→        holistic_cache=review_cache.get("holistic")
   405→        if isinstance(review_cache, dict)
   406→        else None,
   407→        holistic_total_files=len(files),
   408→    )
   409→
   410→    # Also check holistic review staleness.
   411→    holistic_entries = detect_holistic_review_staleness(
   412→        review_cache,
   413→        total_files=len(files),
   414→        max_age_days=max_age,
   415→    )
   416→    entries.extend(holistic_entries)
   417→
   418→    results = _entries_to_findings("subjective_review", entries)
   419→    _log_phase_summary("subjective review", results, potential, "reviewable files")
   420→
   421→    return results, {"subjective_review": potential}
   422→
   423→
   424→def phase_signature(path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract) -> tuple[list[Finding], dict[str, int]]:
   425→    """Shared phase runner: detect signature variance via lang.extract_functions.
   426→
   427→    Backend-agnostic — works with any extractor that returns FunctionInfo objects
   428→    (tree-sitter, regex, AST, etc.).  Returns empty results when the lang has no
   429→    function extractor.
   430→    """
   431→    from desloppify.engine.detectors.signature import detect_signature_variance
   432→
   433→    functions = lang.extract_functions(path)
   434→
   435→    findings: list[Finding] = []
   436→    potentials: dict[str, int] = {}
   437→
   438→    if not functions:
   439→        return findings, potentials
   440→
   441→    entries, _total = detect_signature_variance(functions, min_occurrences=3)
   442→    for e in entries:
   443→        findings.append(make_finding(
   444→            "signature", e["files"][0],
   445→            f"signature_variance::{e['name']}",
   446→            tier=3, confidence="medium",
   447→            summary=(
   448→                f"'{e['name']}' has {e['signature_count']} different signatures "
   449→                f"across {e['file_count']} files"
   450→            ),
   451→        ))
   452→    if entries:
   453→        potentials["signature"] = len(entries)
   454→        log(f"         signature variance: {len(entries)}")
   455→
   456→    return findings, potentials
   457→
   458→
   459→def run_structural_phase(
   460→    path: Path,
   461→    lang: LangRuntimeContract,
   462→    *,
   463→    complexity_signals: list[ComplexitySignal],
   464→    log_fn,
   465→    min_loc: int = 40,
   466→    god_rules=None,
   467→    god_extractor_fn=None,
   468→) -> tuple[list[dict], dict[str, int]]:
   469→    """Run large/complexity/flat directory detectors for a language.
   470→
   471→    Optional ``god_rules`` + ``god_extractor_fn`` enable god-class detection:
   472→    when both are provided, ``god_extractor_fn(path)`` is called to extract
   473→    class info, then ``detect_gods()`` finds classes matching multiple rules.
   474→    """
   475→    structural: dict[str, dict] = {}
   476→
   477→    large_entries, file_count = detect_large_files(
   478→        path,
   479→        file_finder=lang.file_finder,
   480→        threshold=lang.large_threshold,
   481→    )
   482→    for entry in large_entries:
   483→        add_structural_signal(
   484→            structural,
   485→            entry["file"],
   486→            f"large ({entry['loc']} LOC)",
   487→            {"loc": entry["loc"]},
   488→        )
   489→
   490→    complexity_entries, _ = detect_complexity(
   491→        path,
   492→        signals=complexity_signals,
   493→        file_finder=lang.file_finder,
   494→        threshold=lang.complexity_threshold,
   495→        min_loc=min_loc,
   496→    )
   497→    for entry in complexity_entries:
   498→        add_structural_signal(
   499→            structural,
   500→            entry["file"],
   501→            f"complexity score {entry['score']}",
   502→            {"complexity_score": entry["score"], "complexity_signals": entry["signals"]},
   503→        )
   504→        lang.complexity_map[entry["file"]] = entry["score"]
   505→
   506→    if god_rules and god_extractor_fn:
   507→        from desloppify.engine.detectors.gods import detect_gods
   508→
   509→        god_entries, _ = detect_gods(god_extractor_fn(path), god_rules, min_reasons=2)
   510→        for entry in god_entries:
   511→            add_structural_signal(
   512→                structural, entry["file"], entry["signal_text"], entry["detail"],
   513→            )
   514→        if god_entries:
   515→            log_fn(f"         god classes: {len(god_entries)}")
   516→
   517→    results = merge_structural_signals(structural, log_fn)
   518→    flat_entries, analyzed_dir_count = detect_flat_dirs(path, file_finder=lang.file_finder)
   519→    for entry in flat_entries:
   520→        child_dir_count = int(entry.get("child_dir_count", 0))
   521→        combined_score = int(entry.get("combined_score", entry.get("file_count", 0)))
   522→        results.append(
   523→            make_finding(
   524→                "flat_dirs",
   525→                entry["directory"],
   526→                "",
   527→                tier=3,
   528→                confidence="medium",
   529→                summary=format_flat_dir_summary(entry),
   530→                detail={
   531→                    "file_count": entry["file_count"],
   532→                    "child_dir_count": child_dir_count,
   533→                    "combined_score": combined_score,
   534→                    "kind": entry.get("kind", "overload"),
   535→                    "parent_sibling_count": int(entry.get("parent_sibling_count", 0)),
   536→                    "wrapper_item_count": int(entry.get("wrapper_item_count", 0)),
   537→                    "sparse_child_count": int(entry.get("sparse_child_count", 0)),
   538→                    "sparse_child_ratio": float(entry.get("sparse_child_ratio", 0.0)),
   539→                    "sparse_child_file_threshold": int(
   540→                        entry.get("sparse_child_file_threshold", 0)
   541→                    ),
   542→                },
   543→            )
   544→        )
   545→    if flat_entries:
   546→        log_fn(
   547→            f"         flat dirs: {len(flat_entries)} overloaded directories "
   548→            "(files/subdirs/combined)"
   549→        )
   550→
   551→    potentials = {
   552→        "structural": adjust_potential(lang.zone_map, file_count),
   553→        "flat_dirs": analyzed_dir_count,
   554→    }
   555→    return results, potentials
   556→
   557→
   558→def run_coupling_phase(
   559→    path: Path,
   560→    lang: LangRuntimeContract,
   561→    *,
   562→    build_dep_graph_fn,
   563→    log_fn,
   564→    post_process_fn=None,
   565→) -> tuple[list[dict], dict[str, int]]:
   566→    """Run single-use/cycles/orphaned detectors against a language dep graph.
   567→
   568→    Optional ``post_process_fn(findings, entries, lang)`` is called after
   569→    creating single-use and orphaned findings to allow per-language
   570→    adjustments (e.g. confidence gating based on corroboration signals).
   571→    """
   572→    graph = build_dep_graph_fn(path)
   573→    lang.dep_graph = graph
   574→    zone_map = lang.zone_map
   575→    results: list[dict] = []
   576→
   577→    single_entries, single_candidates = detect_single_use_abstractions(
   578→        path,
   579→        graph,
   580→        barrel_names=lang.barrel_names,
   581→    )
   582→    single_entries = filter_entries(zone_map, single_entries, "single_use")
   583→    single_findings = make_single_use_findings(
   584→        single_entries, lang.get_area, stderr_fn=log_fn,
   585→    )
   586→    if post_process_fn:
   587→        post_process_fn(single_findings, single_entries, lang)
   588→    results.extend(single_findings)
   589→
   590→    cycle_entries, _ = detect_cycles(graph)
   591→    cycle_entries = filter_entries(zone_map, cycle_entries, "cycles", file_key="files")
   592→    results.extend(make_cycle_findings(cycle_entries, log_fn))
   593→
   594→    orphan_entries, total_graph_files = detect_orphaned_files(
   595→        path,
   596→        graph,
   597→        extensions=lang.extensions,
   598→        options=OrphanedDetectionOptions(
   599→            extra_entry_patterns=lang.entry_patterns,
   600→            extra_barrel_names=lang.barrel_names,
   601→        ),
   602→    )
   603→    orphan_entries = filter_entries(zone_map, orphan_entries, "orphaned")
   604→    orphan_findings = make_orphaned_findings(orphan_entries, log_fn)
   605→    if post_process_fn:
   606→        post_process_fn(orphan_findings, orphan_entries, lang)
   607→    results.extend(orphan_findings)
   608→
   609→    log_fn(f"         -> {len(results)} coupling/structural findings total")
   610→    potentials = {
   611→        "single_use": adjust_potential(zone_map, single_candidates),
   612→        "cycles": adjust_potential(zone_map, total_graph_files),
   613→        "orphaned": adjust_potential(zone_map, total_graph_files),
   614→    }
   615→    return results, potentials
   616→
   617→
   618→def make_structural_coupling_phase_pair(
   619→    *,
   620→    complexity_signals: list[ComplexitySignal],
   621→    build_dep_graph_fn,
   622→    log_fn,
   623→) -> tuple:
   624→    """Create default structural/coupling phase callables for a language.
   625→
   626→    This keeps language phase modules declarative by letting them provide only
   627→    their complexity signals and dependency-graph builder.
   628→    """
   629→
   630→    def phase_structural(path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract) -> tuple[list[dict], dict[str, int]]:
   631→        return run_structural_phase(
   632→            path,
   633→            lang,
   634→            complexity_signals=complexity_signals,
   635→            log_fn=log_fn,
   636→        )
   637→
   638→    def phase_coupling(path: Path, lang: LangRuntimeContract) -> tuple[list[dict], dict[str, int]]:
   639→        return run_coupling_phase(
   640→            path,
   641→            lang,
   642→            build_dep_graph_fn=build_dep_graph_fn,
   643→            log_fn=log_fn,
   644→        )
   645→
   646→    return phase_structural, phase_coupling
   647→
   648→
   649→__all__ = [
   650→    "find_external_test_files",
   651→    "make_structural_coupling_phase_pair",
   652→    "phase_boilerplate_duplication",
   653→    "phase_dupes",
   654→    "phase_private_imports",
   655→    "phase_security",
   656→    "phase_signature",
   657→    "phase_subjective_review",
   658→    "phase_test_coverage",
   659→    "run_coupling_phase",
   660→    "run_structural_phase",
   661→]
   662→

   252→    def coverage_warnings(self, value: list[DetectorCoverageRecord]) -> None:
   253→        self.state.coverage_warnings = value
   254→
   255→    def __getattr__(self, name: str):
   256→        if name in _FORWARDED_CONFIG_ATTRS:
   257→            return getattr(self.config, name)
   258→        raise AttributeError(
   259→            f"{self.__class__.__name__!s} has no attribute {name!r}; "
   260→            "access runtime state via explicit LangRun properties"
   261→        )
   262→
   263→    def __dir__(self):
   264→        """Expose LangConfig + mutable runtime fields for discoverability."""
   265→        return (
   266→            list(super().__dir__())
   267→            + sorted(_FORWARDED_CONFIG_ATTRS)
   268→            + sorted(_LANG_RUNTIME_STATE_FIELDS)
   269→        )
   270→
   271→    @property
   272→    def large_threshold(self) -> int:
   273→        override = self.state.large_threshold_override
   274→        if isinstance(override, int) and override > 0:
   275→            return override
   276→        return self.config.large_threshold
   277→
   278→    @property
   279→    def props_threshold(self) -> int:
   280→        override = self.state.props_threshold_override
   281→        if isinstance(override, int) and override > 0:
   282→            return override
   283→        return self.config.props_threshold
   284→
   285→    def runtime_setting(self, key: str, default: Any = None) -> Any:
   286→        if key in self.state.runtime_settings:
   287→            return self.state.runtime_settings[key]
   288→        spec = self.config.setting_specs.get(key)
   289→        if spec:
   290→            return copy.deepcopy(spec.default)
   291→        return default
   292→
   293→    def runtime_option(self, key: str, default: Any = None) -> Any:
   294→        if key in self.state.runtime_options:
   295→            return self.state.runtime_options[key]
   296→        spec = self.config.runtime_option_specs.get(key)
   297→        if spec:
   298→            return copy.deepcopy(spec.default)
   299→        return default
   300→
   301→
   302→def _coerce_lang_override(field_name: str, value: object) -> object:
   303→    """Normalize override values to LangRuntimeState-compatible payloads."""
   304→    if field_name in _LANG_OVERRIDE_DICT_FIELDS:
   305→        return value or {}
   306→    if field_name in _LANG_OVERRIDE_LIST_FIELDS:
   307→        return value or []
   308→    if field_name in _LANG_OVERRIDE_INT_FIELDS:
   309→        return int(value or 0)
   310→    if field_name == "review_max_age_days":
   311→        if value is None:
   312→            return None
   313→        return int(value)
   314→    return value
   315→
   316→
   317→def _apply_lang_overrides(runtime: LangRun, overrides: LangRunOverrides) -> None:
   318→    """Apply override bundle to runtime state via one normalized loop."""
   319→    for field_name in _LANG_OVERRIDE_FIELDS:
   320→        value = getattr(overrides, field_name)
   321→        if value is _UNSET:
   322→            continue
   323→        coerced = _coerce_lang_override(field_name, value)
   324→        if field_name == "review_max_age_days" and coerced is None:
   325→            continue
   326→        setattr(runtime, field_name, coerced)
   327→
   328→
   329→def make_lang_run(
   330→    lang: LangConfig | LangRun,
   331→    overrides: LangRunOverrides | None = None,
   332→) -> LangRun:
   333→    """Build a fresh LangRun for a command invocation."""
   334→
   335→    if isinstance(lang, LangRun):
   336→        runtime = lang
   337→    else:
   338→        runtime = LangRun(config=lang)
   339→        runtime.state.runtime_settings = copy.deepcopy(
   340→            getattr(lang, "_default_runtime_settings", {})
   341→        )
   342→        runtime.state.runtime_options = copy.deepcopy(
   343→            getattr(lang, "_default_runtime_options", {})
   344→        )
   345→
   346→    resolved = overrides if overrides is not None else LangRunOverrides()
   347→    _apply_lang_overrides(runtime, resolved)
   348→    return runtime
   349→
   350→
   351→__all__ = [
   352→    "LangRuntimeContract",
   353→    "LangRun",
   354→    "LangRunOverrides",
   355→    "LangRuntimeState",
   356→    "make_lang_run",
   357→]
   358→

   109→def _scan_root_from_files(files: list[str]) -> Path | None:
   110→    """Derive the common ancestor directory from a list of file paths."""
   111→    import os
   112→
   113→    py_files = [f for f in files if f.endswith(".py")]
   114→    if not py_files:
   115→        return None
   116→    try:
   117→        common = Path(os.path.commonpath(py_files))
   118→        return common if common.is_dir() else common.parent
   119→    except ValueError:
   120→        return None

   125→    def _missing_bandit_coverage(self) -> DetectorCoverageStatus:
   126→        return DetectorCoverageStatus(

   141→        if shutil.which("bandit") is not None:

   143→        return [self._missing_bandit_coverage()]
   144→
   145→    def detect_lang_security_detailed(self, files, zone_map) -> LangSecurityResult:
   146→        scan_root = _scan_root_from_files(files)
   147→        if scan_root is None:
   148→            return LangSecurityResult(entries=[], files_scanned=0)
   149→
   150→        exclude_dirs = collect_exclude_dirs(scan_root)
   151→
   152→        result = detect_with_bandit(scan_root, zone_map, exclude_dirs=exclude_dirs)
   153→        coverage = result.status.coverage()
   154→        return LangSecurityResult(
   155→            entries=result.entries,
   156→            files_scanned=result.files_scanned,
   157→            coverage=coverage,
   158→        )

    80→def detect_ts_security(
    81→    files: list[str],
    82→    zone_map: FileZoneMap | None,
    83→) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
    84→    """Detect TypeScript-specific security issues.
    85→
    86→    Returns (entries, files_scanned).

    89→
    90→
    91→def detect_ts_security_result(
    92→    files: list[str],
    93→    zone_map: FileZoneMap | None,
    94→) -> DetectorResult[dict]:
    95→    """Detect TypeScript-specific security issues with explicit result contract."""
    96→    entries: list[dict] = []
    97→    scanned = 0
    98→
    99→    for filepath in files:
   100→        if zone_map is not None:
   101→            zone = zone_map.get(filepath)
   102→            if zone in (Zone.TEST, Zone.CONFIG, Zone.GENERATED, Zone.VENDOR):
   103→                continue
   104→
   105→        try:
   106→            content = Path(filepath).read_text(errors="replace")
   107→        except OSError as exc:
   108→            log_best_effort_failure(
   109→                logger, f"read TypeScript security source {filepath}", exc
   110→            )
   111→            continue
   112→
   113→        scanned += 1
   114→        normalized_path = filepath.replace("\\", "/")
   115→        is_server_only = is_server_only_path(normalized_path)
   116→        lines = content.splitlines()
   117→        has_dev_guard = "__IS_DEV_ENV__" in content or "isDev" in content
   118→
   119→        for line_num, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
   120→            stripped = line.lstrip()
   121→            if stripped.startswith("//"):
   122→                continue
   123→            entries.extend(
   124→                _line_security_findings(
   125→                    filepath=filepath,
   126→                    normalized_path=normalized_path,
   127→                    lines=lines,
   128→                    line_num=line_num,
   129→                    line=line,
   130→                    is_server_only=is_server_only,
   131→                    has_dev_guard=has_dev_guard,
   132→                )
   133→            )
   134→
   135→        entries.extend(
   136→            _file_level_security_findings(
   137→                filepath=filepath,
   138→                normalized_path=normalized_path,
   139→                lines=lines,
   140→                content=content,
   141→            )
   142→        )
   143→
   144→    return DetectorResult(entries=entries, population_kind="files", population_size=scanned)
